title: Perform a minor repair to a metal propeller blade
subject: Powerplant
assumptions: The cleaned surface is left dry, with no solvent pooling or wet film remaining on the blade.
The recorded dimensions are compared against the manufacturer's allowable repair limits and shown to be within them.
The outline is a smooth contoured shape with rounded corners — no sharp points, V-notches or straight-cut corners.
The marked repair area falls within the manufacturer's allowable repair/blend limits for that blade station.
Metal is removed only by hand with riffler/jeweler files, in forward strokes, with no power tool used.
The blended area is rounded in all directions, with no sharp corners, ridges or V-shaped depression.
openQuestions: Every check, error mode and evidence item in this pack was drafted by packs/compile_pack.py from the procedure sheet and handbook, and has not been reviewed by a subject-matter expert.

The procedure sheet cites AC 43.13-1B pp. 8-29 to 8-31; that text was not supplied. A subject-matter expert must supply it and confirm the propeller blade repair limits before this pack is marked reviewed.

The supplied FAA-H-8083-32B extract (pp. 10-44 to 10-47) covers turbine compressor and inducer blades, not metal propeller blades, and is not cited by the procedure sheet. Confirm whether it should be cited at all or replaced with a propeller section.

No numeric allowable depth, length or width limit for a minor metal propeller blade repair appears in any supplied text. What limit does the student check against, and from which manufacturer document?

Does this task require post-repair NDI (magnetic particle or fluorescent penetrant) to confirm all traces of damage are removed? The assumed handbook extract requires it for compressor blades; the procedure sheet does not mention it.
Is the repair area required to be re-protected (primer, paint, corrosion-preventive) after blending, and if so should that be an evidence item?

subtasks.label: Prepare the Damaged Area
subtasks.excluded: 1 [video], 4 [document], 3 [measurement] — held beside the frame, never folded into the criterion.

steps.text: Clean the portion of the blade to be repaired.

checks.text: The area around the damage is free of oil, grease, dirt and debris, with clean bare metal exposed.
checks.src: Senior Mechanic Note 1: wipe 'to remove oils, dirt, and debris' before damage assessment.

checks.text: The damage boundary is clearly discernible, not obscured by smeared solvent, residue or streaking.
checks.src: Cleaning must let the next step verify extent of damage with scale and depth gauge.

checks.text: Wiping is performed with a rag dampened — not saturated — with solvent, not a dry or abrasive wipe.
checks.src: Senior Mechanic Note 1 specifies 'a rag dampened with solvent'; only observable while the action is performed.

checks.text: The solvent used is approved for the blade alloy and its SDS handling requirements are met.
checks.src: 'Use all relevant data... to include the Type Certificate Data Sheet (TCDS), Safety Data Sheet' and service manuals.

checks.text: The cleaned surface is left dry, with no solvent pooling or wet film remaining on the blade.
checks.src: Handbook: 'Cleaning parts by the chlorinated solvent method leaves the parts absolutely dry.' Assumed reference (turbine parts); needs SME confirmation.

errors.text: Oil or grime film left in the damage, hiding cracks and depth so the blade looks acceptably clean.
Scrubbing with abrasive pad, wire brush or file instead of a solvent-dampened rag, adding scratches.
Excess solvent left standing on the blade or run onto adjacent coatings and seals.

steps.text: Verify the extent of the damage.

checks.text: With the plunger on an undamaged flat area of the blade, the depth gauge reads zero before any damage measurement is taken.
checks.src: Sheet: place gauge on a flat surface, loosen dial clamping screw and rotate needle to zero before reading.

checks.text: Recorded damage depth is taken with the gauge centered on the deepest point and read to 0.001" resolution.
checks.src: Sheet specifies centering over the deepest part; dial ring lines are 0.001", small dial 0.1".

checks.text: Length, width and depth of the damage are all recorded in writing before any material is removed.
checks.src: Sheet requires steel scale for length and width, depth gauge for depth; pen and paper listed as equipment.

checks.text: The recorded dimensions are compared against the manufacturer's allowable repair limits and shown to be within them.
checks.src: Handbook: "may be repaired if the damage can be removed without exceeding the allowable limits established by the manufacturer"; extract is uncited and addresses compressor blades — needs SME confirmation.

errors.text: Gauge zeroed on a curved or damaged area, so the recorded depth is understated while the paperwork looks complete.
Damage measured without checking it against manufacturer allowable limits, so an unrepairable blade is blended anyway.
Only length and width taken; depth omitted or estimated visually rather than with the depth gauge.
Dimensions read but not written down, so the post-repair comparison cannot be made.

checks.text: A closed dye or marker outline is visible on the blade and fully encircles all of the identified damage.
checks.src: Sheet: "Outline the repair area with dye or a marker." Outline must contain the damage found in step 2.

checks.text: The outline is a smooth contoured shape with rounded corners — no sharp points, V-notches or straight-cut corners.
checks.src: Sheet: "Draw a contoured shape that tapers into the damage." Handbook (provisional): damage "of a rounded or gradual contour type and not a sharp or V-type."

checks.text: The outline extends beyond the recorded damage length and width, leaving margin for a taper on all sides.
checks.src: Requires comparing outline dimensions to the length/width/depth recorded with steel scale and depth gauge in step 2.

checks.text: The marked repair area falls within the manufacturer's allowable repair/blend limits for that blade station.
checks.src: "may be repaired if the damage can be removed without exceeding the allowable limits established by the manufacturer" — uncited extract, needs SME confirmation.

checks.text: The blade surface shows no scribe, punch or scratch marks used as marking, only dye or ink.
checks.src: Sheet permits only "dye or a marker"; mechanical marking would add a stress riser to the repair area.

errors.text: Outline drawn with sharp corners or a V-shape, seeding a stress concentration in the blended repair.
Outline drawn tight to the damage edge with no taper margin, so blending cannot fair into the blade.
Part of the damage (e.g., a crack extension or adjacent nick) left outside the outline.
Marking line so heavy or smeared that the damage boundary is obscured.

sheetPoints.text: Damaged area and surrounding blade surface show clean bare metal, free of oil, dirt and debris
Damage outline is clearly visible and not obscured by residue, smears or streaking
No standing solvent, wet film or drip runs on the blade surface
No new scratch or scuff pattern from abrasive cleaning in the cleaned area
Depth gauge base is seated flat on the blade with the plunger positioned over the damage
Dial face is legible and unobstructed in the frame
Steel scale is laid along the damage spanning its full length/width
Damaged area is clean and unaltered (no filing or sanding evident yet)
A closed dye/marker outline is present and surrounds all visible damage
Outline is smoothly contoured with rounded corners; no sharp points or V-notches
Outline is drawn clear of the damage edge, not traced on it
No scribe, punch or scratch marks on the blade; marking is ink/dye only
Marking line is crisp and does not obscure the damage itself

subtasks.label: Blend the Damage Out
subtasks.excluded: 7 [video], 2 [measurement], 1 [document] — held beside the frame, never folded into the criterion.

steps.text: File the rough edges of the damage down.

checks.text: The perimeter of the damage shows no visible burrs, raised lips or torn metal after filing.
checks.src: Sheet: "Edges should feel flush with no burrs or raised points"; visible raised metal is disqualifying.

checks.text: Filed edges feel flush to the fingertip with no catch or raised point when checked by hand.
checks.src: Tactile flushness cannot be settled from a still; must be watched being verified.

checks.text: Filing is confined inside the marked repair outline, with no file marks or scoring on undamaged blade surface.
checks.src: Sheet has student outline the repair area and taper into damage; work stays within that outline.

checks.text: Metal is removed only by hand with riffler/jeweler files, in forward strokes, with no power tool used.
checks.src: Handbook: "Re-work must be accomplished by hand, using stones, files, or emery cloth. Do not use a power tool" — compressor-blade text, needs SME confirmation.

errors.text: Back-and-forth or cross filing leaves transverse scratches across the blade, creating stress risers that look smooth to a novice.
Filing extends outside the marked outline or removes excess depth, thinning the blade beyond allowable limits.
A burr or raised lip is left on the perimeter of the damage, requiring rework.

checks.text: The blended area is rounded in all directions, with no sharp corners, ridges or V-shaped depression.
checks.src: Sheet: "round the repair in all directions"; handbook: damage "of a rounded or gradual contour type and not a sharp or V-type" — assumed reference, needs SME confirmation.

checks.text: Contouring is confined to the previously marked repair outline, with no filing marks outside it.
checks.src: Prep step required an outlined, tapered repair area; contouring must stay inside that dye/marker boundary.

checks.text: Depth of metal removed by contouring does not exceed the manufacturer's allowable blade repair limit.
checks.src: "may be repaired if the damage can be removed without exceeding the allowable limits established by the manufacturer"; extract covers compressor blades — provisional, SME confirmation needed.

checks.text: Contouring is done by hand with a riffler or jeweler file only; no power tool is used on the blade.
checks.src: Sheet specifies riffler/jeweler file; handbook: "Re-work must be accomplished by hand... Do not use a power tool" — assumed reference, provisional.

errors.text: Repair is filed into a sharp-cornered or V-shaped depression that looks smooth but forms a stress riser.
Over-filing removes metal beyond allowable depth, thinning the blade section.
File strokes run across the blade or stray outside the marked outline, leaving gouges and scored metal.

steps.text: Taper the repair into the blade shape.

checks.text: The blend boundary is a gradual rounded contour with no sharp corners, V-notches or abrupt outline changes.
checks.src: Procedure sheet: "No sharp shapes." Handbook (assumed): "rounded or gradual contour type and not a sharp or V-type" — needs SME confirmation for propellers.

checks.text: Repair edges are flush with the undamaged blade, with no detectable step, ridge or raised lip when a fingertip is drawn across.
checks.src: Sheet requires "a smooth transition to the undamaged portions of the blade"; flushness is tactile, not visible in a still.

checks.text: Tapering is done by hand with riffler/jeweler files worked along the blade length, with no power tools used.
checks.src: "Re-work must be accomplished by hand, using stones, files, or emery cloth. Do not use a power tool" — provisional, extract covers compressor blades.

checks.text: Depth of material removed by the taper stays within the manufacturer's allowable repair limits for the blade.
checks.src: "if the damage can be removed without exceeding the allowable limits established by the manufacturer" — provisional; limits come from propeller manual/TCDS.

errors.text: Taper ends in a sharp-edged or V-shaped notch at the blend boundary, concentrating stress while looking repaired.
Excess material filed away chasing the taper, exceeding allowable blade depth limits.
Abrupt step or ridge left where the repair meets undamaged blade, requiring rework.
Cross-filing marks left running across rather than along the blade length.

checks.text: The sanded repair area shows a uniform fine finish with no remaining file marks, coarse scratches or discoloration.
checks.src: Sheet: "leveling the repair"; handbook (assumed page range): "surface finish in the repaired area must be comparable to that of a new blade."

checks.text: A hand passed over the repair detects no raised textures, ridges or edges at the transition to undamaged blade.
checks.src: Sheet: "Feel for raised textures" — tactile flushness judgement, not settleable from a still image.

checks.text: Sanding is done by hand with abrasive worked parallel to blade length; no power tool or buffer is used.
checks.src: "performed parallel to the length of the blade... Do not use a power tool" — assumed reference, needs SME confirmation.

checks.text: The final abrasive used is #00 (extra fine) grit as specified for this task.
checks.src: Sheet: "Progress to a #00 grit sandpaper"; grit grade is established from the abrasive spec/label, not the surface.

errors.text: Sanding continues past blend-out, thinning the blade beyond allowable depth while the surface still looks smooth and finished.
Power tool or rotary buffing used to level the area, removing excess material and altering blade temper.
Coarse scratches or a raised ridge remain at the repair perimeter, leaving a visible unblended edge.
Abrasive strokes run across (transverse to) blade length, leaving cross-grain scratch lines.

sheetPoints.text: Perimeter of the damaged area shows no visible burrs, raised lips or torn metal
File marks and material removal stay inside the marked repair outline
No scoring, gouges or scratches on undamaged blade surface adjacent to the repair
Repair perimeter shows uniform hand-file texture, no rotary/power-tool swirl marks
Blended area shows a rounded, dish-like contour in all directions with no sharp corners or ridges
No V-shaped or angular depression visible in the repair
Filing confined within the marked repair outline; surrounding blade surface unmarked
No visible gouges, chatter marks or cross-blade scoring in the contoured area
Blend boundary is a gradual rounded contour, no sharp corners or V-shaped notches visible
Repair area fairs smoothly into the surrounding blade profile with no visible abrupt edge line
No gouges, sharp facets or cross-blade file scoring inside the blended area
Repair area shows a uniform extra-fine finish with no file marks or coarse scratch lines
No visible ridge, step or outline where the repair meets undamaged blade surface
Scratch pattern in the repaired area runs lengthwise along the blade, not across it
Repair area free of remaining dents, pits or dark damage traces

subtasks.label: Clean the Repair
subtasks.excluded: 2 [video], 1 [measurement], 1 [document] — held beside the frame, never folded into the criterion.

checks.text: The repair area and adjacent blade surface show no visible metallic dust, filings or swarf.
checks.src: Senior Mechanic Note: 'Clear all fine metallic dust from the blade surface with a rag dampened with solvent.'

checks.text: Wiping is done with a rag dampened with cleaning solvent, not a dry or contaminated rag.
checks.src: Note specifies a solvent-dampened rag; dampening cannot be judged from a still of the finished blade.

checks.text: No solvent pooling, streaks or lint remain on the blade and the surface is left dry.
checks.src: Handbook: 'Cleaning parts by the chlorinated solvent method leaves the parts absolutely dry.' Uncited page range; needs SME confirmation.

checks.text: With dust removed, the blended repair reads as a smooth finish comparable to the surrounding undamaged blade.
checks.src: Handbook: 'The surface finish in the repaired area must be comparable to that of a new blade.' Provisional, uncited reference; confirm with SME.

errors.text: Dust is smeared or packed into the repair rather than removed, leaving a clean-looking blade with grit that falsifies the follow-on depth measurement.
Blade wiped dry or with a soiled rag, leaving metallic dust and oils on the surface.
Excess solvent, lint or wipe streaks left on the blade face.

steps.text: Measure the dimensions of the repair.

checks.text: Length, width and depth of the finished repair are each measured and recorded as numeric values.
checks.src: Sheet: "Use a steel scale to measure the length and width of the repair. Use a depth gauge to measure the depth of the repair."

checks.text: Depth gauge is zeroed on a flat area of the blade and its plunger centered over the deepest point of the repair.
checks.src: Sheet gauge procedure: zero the needle on a flat surface, "Center the gauge over the deepest part of the damage."

checks.text: Depth gauge base sits flat and fully seated on the blade surface, not tilted or bridging the blend.
checks.src: Sheet: "Place the depth gauge on a flat surface of the blade"; tilted seating invalidates the reading.

checks.text: Recorded repair dimensions are compared against the manufacturer's allowable repair limits and shown to be within them.
checks.src: Handbook: repair permitted "without exceeding the allowable limits established by the manufacturer"; extract covers compressor blades — needs SME confirmation for propellers.

errors.text: Depth reading taken with the gauge tilted or zeroed on a curved area, understating actual material removal.
Repair depth exceeds the manufacturer's allowable limit but is recorded as acceptable, leaving a plausible-looking blade unairworthy.
Dimensions estimated or omitted, so no record exists of final repair size for the maintenance entry.
Dial misread by one small-dial increment (0.1"), giving a wrong but plausible depth figure.

sheetPoints.text: Repair area and surrounding blade free of visible metallic dust, filings or swarf
Blade surface left dry with no solvent pooling, streaks or lint
Blended repair appears smooth and continuous with the undamaged blade surface
Loose metal debris collected in the FOD box, not left on the bench or blade
Steel scale is laid across the repair spanning its full length/width with graduations against the blended edges
Depth gauge base rests flat and fully contacting the blade, plunger over the deepest part of the repair
Repair area is free of metallic dust and solvent residue where the tools contact it
